interactions.label: Filter
interactions.teaches: Compares the smooth, bell-shaped binomial filter with the flat box filter of equivalent total volume (DC gain = 16)

interactions.label: Show Separability
interactions.teaches: Reveals how the 2D filter is formed by multiplying a 1D [1, 2, 1] horizontal filter with a 1D [1, 2, 1] vertical filter

demo_steps.title: The Binomial Filter b_2,2
demo_steps.narration: This is the 2D binomial filter kernel. Its coefficients peak at 4 in the center, taper to 2 at the edges, and fall to 1 at the corners, summing to a total DC volume of 16. This smooth, isotropic-like shape performs gentle, high-quality blurring.

demo_steps.title: Separable construction
demo_steps.narration: By enabling separability, we see that the 2D grid is simply the outer product of two 1D [1, 2, 1] binomial filters. This means we can filter an image incredibly fast: first filter along the rows, then along the columns.

demo_steps.title: Comparison with Box Filter
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the Box Filter, all nine coefficients are flat-topped at 1.78 (so the total sum remains 16). Because of its abrupt, sharp rectangular edges, the box filter cannot perfectly eliminate high-frequency checkerboard noise, whereas the smooth binomial filter can.
